newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Star shares in limbo over court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Star shares in limbo over court ruling.

text.p: Star Mining Corp NL said on Monday its shares would remain suspended while it attempts to clarify its position in the Sukhoi Log gold project in Russia following a court ruling that could effect the project.

Star Mining said the Supreme Arbitration Court of Russia in Moscow, has declared the Founding Agreement of the August 27 1992 on the establishment of the joint stock company (JSC) Lenzoloto and Lenzoloto's company charter, null and void.
Last month, Star Mining, which holds 34.88 percent of Lenzoloto, said it would acquire 49 percent of Sukhoi Log Mining Co, which shares the rights to develop the Sukhoi deposit.

Star Mining said the Russian court also declared null and void the Certificate of Registration of JSC Lenzoloto and the inclusion into the Share Register of Enterprises, issued by the Committee of Foreign Investments with the Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation.
"Furthermore the court ruled that the key elements of this decision could not be appealed," Star said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange.
"It is not clear at this stage what effect the court decision on JSC Lenzoloto has on Star," it said.
Sukhoi Log Mining has a share of the rights to develop the Sukhoi Log gold field, which has been dubbed "Siberia's El Dorado", with gold reserves of about 35 million troy ounces.

The acquisition of 49 percent of Sukhoi Log by Star Mining's unit Star Technology would lead to a restructure of Lenzoloto. In February, a Lenzoloto offical said Star Mining was the preferred bidder for the shares in Sukhoi Log Mining Co.

Last November, Star Mining formed a deal with South African mining group JCI Ltd for JCI to acquire an option to subscribe for shares in Star Technology for about US$250 million giving it a 30 percent economic interest in Sukhoi Log.
Star has said subject to agreement between JCI and Star, funding for Star's acquisition of its Sukhoi Log Mining Co had been agreed with Standard Bank of South Africa.
Under the terms of the agreement, Standard Bank would provide US$50 million on April 21 to purchase the interest in the Sukhoi Log Mining Co said Star Mining.
Star Mining said it was also arranging finance from Standard Bank for the Sukhoi Log project for no less than US$700 million.
"This new contradictory ruling therefore comes at a time when the initial funding of the project is close to fulfilment," Star said.
Star has said Lenzoloto has made guarantees to Star that the restructuring of Lenzoloto, the formation of Sukhoi Log Mining Co and Star's acquisition would be completed by April 21.
Star shares were suspened at the company's request earlier on Monday. The shares last traded at 18 cents, down two cents on Friday's close. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
